- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

#!/bin/bash
set -e
# Run all verification experiments and report results
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

echo "Running CPAchecker verification experiments..."
echo "================================================"

BENCHMARKS_DIR="benchmarks"
RESULTS=()
PASS_COUNT=0
TOTAL=0

run_experiment() {
    local program="$1"
    local config="$2"
    local expected="$3"
    local name="$4"

    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
    local start_time=$(python3 -c "import time; print(time.time())")
    local output
    output=$(python3 cpachecker_main.py --config "$config" --stats "$BENCHMARKS_DIR/$program" 2>&1) || true
    local end_time=$(python3 -c "import time; print(time.time())")
    local elapsed=$(python3 -c "print(f'{$end_time - $start_time:.3f}')")

    local verdict="UNKNOWN"
    if echo "$output" | grep -q "Verification result: TRUE"; then
        verdict="TRUE"
    elif echo "$output" | grep -q "Verification result: FALSE"; then
        verdict="FALSE"
    fi

    local status="FAIL"
    if [ "$verdict" == "$expected" ]; then
        status="PASS"
        PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1))
    fi

    echo "${name}: ${verdict} (expected ${expected}) [${elapsed}s] - ${status}"
    RESULTS+=("${name}: ${verdict}")
}

# Value Analysis experiments (cpachecker_v0)
echo ""
echo "--- Value Analysis (cpachecker_v0) ---"
run_experiment "simple_safe.c" "valueAnalysis" "TRUE" "VA_SIMPLE_SAFE"
run_experiment "simple_unsafe.c" "valueAnalysis" "FALSE" "VA_SIMPLE_UNSAFE"
run_experiment "loop_safe.c" "valueAnalysis" "TRUE" "VA_LOOP_SAFE"
run_experiment "loop_unsafe.c" "valueAnalysis" "FALSE" "VA_LOOP_UNSAFE"

# Predicate Analysis experiments (cpachecker_v1)
echo ""
echo "--- Predicate Analysis (cpachecker_v1) ---"
run_experiment "nondet_safe.c" "predicateAnalysis" "TRUE" "PA_NONDET_SAFE"
run_experiment "nondet_unsafe.c" "predicateAnalysis" "FALSE" "PA_NONDET_UNSAFE"
run_experiment "predicate_safe.c" "predicateAnalysis" "TRUE" "PA_PRED_SAFE"
run_experiment "predicate_unsafe.c" "predicateAnalysis" "FALSE" "PA_PRED_UNSAFE"

# k-Induction and BMC experiments (cpachecker_v3)
echo ""
echo "--- k-Induction & BMC (cpachecker_v3) ---"
run_experiment "induction_safe.c" "kInduction" "TRUE" "KI_INDUCTION_SAFE"
run_experiment "induction_unsafe.c" "kInduction" "FALSE" "KI_INDUCTION_UNSAFE"
run_experiment "bmc_safe.c" "bmc-incremental" "TRUE" "BMC_SAFE"
run_experiment "bmc_unsafe.c" "bmc-incremental" "FALSE" "BMC_UNSAFE"

echo ""
echo "================================================"
echo "Results: ${PASS_COUNT}/${TOTAL} correct"

# Output in expected format
echo ""
echo "--- EXPERIMENT RESULTS ---"
echo "VA_SIMPLE_SAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[0]}" == "VA_SIMPLE_SAFE: TRUE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "VA_SIMPLE_UNSAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[1]}" == "VA_SIMPLE_UNSAFE: FALSE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "VA_LOOP_SAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[2]}" == "VA_LOOP_SAFE: TRUE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "VA_LOOP_UNSAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[3]}" == "VA_LOOP_UNSAFE: FALSE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "PA_NONDET_SAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[4]}" == "PA_NONDET_SAFE: TRUE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "PA_NONDET_UNSAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[5]}" == "PA_NONDET_UNSAFE: FALSE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "PA_PRED_SAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[6]}" == "PA_PRED_SAFE: TRUE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "PA_PRED_UNSAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[7]}" == "PA_PRED_UNSAFE: FALSE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "KI_INDUCTION_SAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[8]}" == "KI_INDUCTION_SAFE: TRUE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "KI_INDUCTION_UNSAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[9]}" == "KI_INDUCTION_UNSAFE: FALSE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "BMC_SAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[10]}" == "BMC_SAFE: TRUE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "BMC_UNSAFE_CORRECT: $( [ "${RESULTS[11]}" == "BMC_UNSAFE: FALSE" ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
echo "TOTAL_CORRECT: ${PASS_COUNT}"
echo "TOTAL_BENCHMARKS: ${TOTAL}"

id: "cpachecker_v0"
title: "CPA Worklist Algorithm with Value Analysis"
category: software_verification
requirement: |-
  ## Context
  CPAchecker is a configurable software verification framework based on the
  Configurable Program Analysis (CPA) concept. The core idea is that different
  verification techniques (value analysis, predicate abstraction, etc.) can be
  expressed as instances of the CPA interface, and a generic worklist algorithm
  (CPA algorithm) explores the reachable abstract state space.

  You are given a Python skeleton that defines: CFA (control-flow automaton)
  data structures, CPA interfaces (AbstractState, TransferRelation, MergeOperator,
  StopOperator), a C parser, and an expression evaluator. Your task is to implement
  the CPA worklist algorithm and two concrete CPAs for value analysis.

  ## Module: cpachecker/analyses/value_analysis.py

  Implement:
  1. **LocationCPA** - Tracks the current program location (CFA node). The abstract
     state is simply the node ID. Transfer relation moves to successor nodes.
     Merge is "sep" (never merge). Stop checks exact coverage.

  2. **ExplicitValueCPA** - Tracks concrete integer values for all variables.
     The abstract state maps variable names to integer values (or TOP for unknown).
     Transfer relation evaluates assignments concretely and checks assume-edges
     for feasibility. Merge is "sep". Stop checks if a state is already covered
     (all variables have same or less-precise values).

  3. **CompositeCPA** - Combines LocationCPA and ExplicitValueCPA into a product
     analysis. The composite state is a tuple of component states. Transfer,
     merge, and stop are applied component-wise.

  4. **CPA Worklist Algorithm** - The main reachability algorithm:
     - Maintain a worklist (frontier) and a reached set
     - Pop a state from worklist, compute successors via transfer relation
     - For each successor, apply merge with all states in reached at same location
     - Apply stop to check coverage; if not covered, add to worklist and reached
     - If an error location is reached, report FALSE (property violation)
     - If worklist is empty, report TRUE (property holds)

  5. **run_value_analysis(cfa, timelimit)** - Entry point that:
     - Creates the CompositeCPA with LocationCPA + ExplicitValueCPA
     - Runs the CPA algorithm on the given CFA
     - Returns a VerificationResult with verdict TRUE/FALSE

  ## Experiments
  The following benchmarks must produce correct results:
  - VA_SIMPLE_SAFE: simple_safe.c with valueAnalysis config -> TRUE
  - VA_SIMPLE_UNSAFE: simple_unsafe.c with valueAnalysis config -> FALSE
  - VA_LOOP_SAFE: loop_safe.c with valueAnalysis config -> TRUE
  - VA_LOOP_UNSAFE: loop_unsafe.c with valueAnalysis config -> FALSE

  ## Instructions
  - Use Python 3 with no external dependencies beyond the standard library
  - Follow the CPA interface defined in cpachecker/cpa_interface.py
  - Use the expression evaluator in cpachecker/expression.py for evaluating C expressions
  - The CFA is already parsed; work with the CFANode/CFAEdge structures from cpachecker/cfa.py
  - Error locations have is_error=True on the CFANode

  ## Files to modify
  - cpachecker/analyses/value_analysis.py (create new)
  - cpachecker/analyses/__init__.py (may need update)

  ## Acceptance signals
  - run.sh outputs VA_SIMPLE_SAFE_CORRECT: 1
  - run.sh outputs VA_SIMPLE_UNSAFE_CORRECT: 1
  - run.sh outputs VA_LOOP_SAFE_CORRECT: 1
  - run.sh outputs VA_LOOP_UNSAFE_CORRECT: 1

"""Control-Flow Automaton (CFA) representation.

A CFA is a directed graph where:
- Nodes represent program locations (program counter values)
- Edges represent program operations (assignments, assumptions, assertions)

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any


class EdgeType(Enum):
    ASSIGNMENT = "assignment"
    ASSUME_TRUE = "assume_true"
    ASSUME_FALSE = "assume_false"
    ASSERT = "assert"
    FUNCTION_CALL = "function_call"
    BLANK = "blank"


@dataclass
class CFANode:
    node_id: int
    label: str = ""
    is_entry: bool = False
    is_exit: bool = False
    is_error: bool = False


@dataclass
class CFAEdge:
    source: int
    target: int
    edge_type: EdgeType
    expression: str = ""
    variable: str = ""
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class CFA:
    """Control-Flow Automaton representing a program."""

    nodes: dict[int, CFANode] = field(default_factory=dict)
    edges: list[CFAEdge] = field(default_factory=list)
    entry_node: int = 0
    exit_node: int = -1
    variables: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    function_name: str = "main"

    def add_node(self, node: CFANode) -> None:
        self.nodes[node.node_id] = node

    def add_edge(self, edge: CFAEdge) -> None:
        self.edges.append(edge)

    def get_successors(self, node_id: int) -> list[CFAEdge]:
        return [e for e in self.edges if e.source == node_id]

    def get_predecessors(self, node_id: int) -> list[CFAEdge]:
        return [e for e in self.edges if e.target == node_id]
